title: From Code Review Comments to Reuse in Production: An Industrial Study of Extracted Rules
title_zh: 从代码审查评论到生产环境复用：规则提取的工业实证研究
abstract_en: Much organization-specific code review knowledge remains embedded in comments on individual changes, and recent systems reuse it by turning those comments into rules a language model applies to later changes. Teams must then decide which rules to keep, and the evidence at hand is how often the system's later comments name each rule. Tracing the rules of one such system, Kleene, through 65 days of production use, we found that such a count does not show what a rule contributed. A rule attribution indicates neither whether the source content was preserved nor whether the comment requested a change. Of 56 clauses in 12 rules that later comments named as their reason, 2 were explicit in a source review thread, 38 added conditions to a corresponding passage, and 16 had no passage we could locate; 45 of 79 further comments naming those rules requested no change, 27 of them while stating that the rule applied. On 20 constructed code changes, a reviewer model given only the unedited source thread met the detection criteria on 8 of the 10 that require a report, against 10 of 10 with the extracted rule, a difference whose confidence interval includes zero. Stage counts locate where rules drop out but not why: of 464 rules deployed while the rule-based reviewer subagent ran in their repository, 259 (55.8%) were named, 195 (42.0%) produced a comment that was not withheld, and 94 (20.3%) one with a recorded code change; the largest reduction occurred before any rule was named. Nor did the deployment-time properties we tested settle the choice in advance: retaining the top-ranked half preserved 53.8% of the rules that later produced a non-withheld comment, against 49.2% at random, a difference whose confidence interval includes zero. Judging extracted rules therefore calls for recording each stage separately and comparing each rule against the threads it was extracted from.
abstract_zh: 组织内部的代码审查经验往往散落在针对单次变更的评论中。Kleene 等系统将这些评论提炼为规则，供语言模型审查后续变更。研究追踪了 Kleene 在生产环境中 65 天的使用情况，发现评论提及某条规则的次数并不能说明该规则的贡献：被提及既不意味着规则忠实于原始讨论，也不意味着评论要求修改代码。在后续评论引用的 12 条规则所含的 56 个条款中，仅 2 个在原始审查讨论中有明确表述，38 个在对应内容上增加了条件，另有 16 个找不到对应内容。在随后引用这些规则的 79 条评论中，45 条没有要求修改，其中 27 条仍明确声称规则适用。研究还构造了 20 个代码变更；在 10 个应报告问题的变更上，仅提供未经编辑的原始讨论时，审查模型有 8 个达到检测标准，提供提取后的规则时则为 10 个，但差值的置信区间包含零。在审查子代理运行期间部署的 464 条规则中，259 条（55.8%）被提及，195 条（42.0%）至少产生了一条未被拦截的评论，94 条（20.3%）至少产生了一条伴随有记录的代码修改的评论。数量降幅最大的阶段发生在规则首次被提及之前，但阶段计数无法解释原因。按部署时可观测的属性排序并保留前一半，可保住后来产生未被拦截评论的规则中的 53.8%，随机保留则为 49.2%，差值的置信区间同样包含零。作者因此建议分别记录各阶段结果，并逐条对照规则与其来源讨论。
key_points_zh: 提取可能改变原意：56 个条款中仅 2 个由原始讨论明确提出，38 个增加了条件，16 个找不到对应内容。
引用不等于要求修改：79 条引用规则的评论中，45 条未要求修改，其中 27 条仍声称规则适用。
原始讨论是值得比较的基线：在 10 个应报告问题的构造案例中，原始讨论和提取规则分别检出 8 个和 10 个，差值的置信区间包含零。
分阶段追踪能定位流失，不能解释原因：464 条规则中，259 条被提及，195 条产生未被拦截的评论，94 条的评论伴随有记录的代码修改。
部署时排序未显示出明确优势：保留排名前一半与随机保留的覆盖率分别为 53.8% 和 49.2%，差值的置信区间包含零。
